links.outcome: LLM extraction errors including hallucinations and wrong-test or wrong-date reports in clinical notes
links.effect: MMSE: LlaMA-2 had 27 total hallucinations, 19 wrong-test, 25 missed scores, 23 wrong dates; ChatGPT had 3 hallucinations, 17 wrong-test, 19 wrong dates.
links.quote: LlaMA-2 errors included 27 cases of total hallucination, 19 cases of reporting other scores instead of MMSE, 25 missed scores, and 23 cases of reporting only the wrong date.

links.outcome: LLM extraction accuracy against expert-reviewer reference standard
links.effect: MMSE accuracy 83% (ChatGPT) vs 66.4% (LlaMA-2); CDR accuracy 87.1% vs 74.5%; CDR precision 48.3% vs 16.1%.
links.quote: For MMSE information extraction, ChatGPT (vs. LlaMA-2) achieved accuracy of 83% (vs. 66.4%), sensitivity of 89.7% (vs. 69.9%), true-negative rates of 96% (vs 60.0%), and precision of 82.7% (vs 62.2%).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation comparing the extraction accuracy and hallucination rates of two LLMs (ChatGPT and LLaMA-2) on retrospective clinical notes without evaluating a specific operational guardrail or deployment practice.
